svg.aria-label: The LEGB lookup order: local -> the enclosing function -> global -> builtin; a closure puts the outer variables in cells, which the function can still reach away from where it was defined
svg.text: Global: the names in the module
Enclosing: the outer function's locals (a closure cell)
The lookup starts innermost and moves out; an assignment creates a local name (nonlocal for the enclosing one, global for the module's)
A closure: the inner function refers to outer variables, which Python puts in cells that __closure__ points at - decorators, callbacks and factories rest on this
The classic trap: lambdas defined in a loop all refer to one cell and all hold the last value afterwards; the default argument i=i fixes it
